bug_report_content:
id: 759
status: Fixed
summary: String conversion optimization is incorrect
labels: ['Type-Defect', 'Priority-Medium']
stars: 0
commentCount: 11
Comment 0 (2012-06-19): What steps will reproduce the problem? var f = { valueOf: function() { return undefined; } } String(f) What is the expected output? What do you see instead? Expected output: "[object Object]" Actual output: "undefined" What version of the product are you using? On what operating system? All versions (http://closure-compiler.appspot.com/ as well). Please provide any additional information below. The compiler optimizes String(x) calls by replacing them with x + ''. This is correct in most cases, but incorrect in corner cases like the one mentioned above.
Comment 1 (2012-06-20): The code sample violates the assumption "Standard methods on Object, Array, String, Number and Boolean have not be redefined in a way that breaks the original contract" [1]. [1] http://code.google.com/p/closure-compiler/wiki/CompilerAssumptions
Comment 2 (2012-06-20): It's not actually breaking the valueOf contract: it takes no arguments, returns a string and has no side effects. It just looks like that the assumption the compiler currently makes: String(Foo) = Foo + '' isn't always valid. The question remains, how high of a priority is such a case?
Comment 3 (2012-06-20): The valueOf method from the code sample does not return a String value but an undefined value (unless another assumption is violated). What is being understood as the contract here? The specification reads: 1. The object initialiser creates "a new object as if by the expression new Object() where Object is the standard built-in constructor with that name". http://ecma-international.org/ecma-262/5.1/#sec-11.1.5 2. When called with no arguments, the Object constructor returns a "native ECMAScript object". http://ecma-international.org/ecma-262/5.1/#sec-15.2.2.1 3. Object.prototype.valueOf returns the "result of calling ToObject passing the this value as the argument" since the this value is not a host object. http://ecma-international.org/ecma-262/5.1/#sec-15.2.4.4 4. When the abstract operation ToObject is called with an argument of the type Object, the "result is the input argument" [4] (i.e. the constructed native ECMAScript object). http://ecma-international.org/ecma-262/5.1/#sec-9.9 It could thereby be concluded that when it comes to the code sample, the valueOf should return the initialised object. var f = {}; f.valueOf = function() { return f; }; String(f); This returns "[object Object]". The Closure Compiler transforms this program into var f={valueOf:function(){return f}};""+f; which also returns "[object Object]".
Comment 4 (2012-06-21): +1 for getting rid of this "optimization". It doesn't really help, and is wrong.
